constraints.form_hypothesis: Schmeh's own assessment: '16th century encryption systems were not especially secure... Some knowledge of ancient German or Latin might be more helpful than codebreaking skills'; he also flags the alternative that this is not an encryption at all but 'an abbreviated text, a meaningless letter sequence, or something else' -- the heavy periods-after-tokens pattern (constraints.alphabet) is exactly what a real 16th-century Latin/German abbreviation convention (not a cipher) looks like, and should be tested against that reading before assuming substitution

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Test the abbreviation hypothesis first, cheaply and without cryptanalysis: compare the token-and-period pattern (short Latin/German-looking fragments each closed with a period, occasional digits) against known 16th-century German/Latin scribal abbreviation conventions (e.g. standard Tironian-note-derived and suspension abbreviations) rather than assuming a substitution cipher -- Schmeh's own text already leans this way ('some knowledge of ancient German or Latin might be more helpful than codebreaking skills'). Cost $1, Sonnet.

2. Fetch Untersberg-Code.png (scienceblogs.de) and the higher-quality archivmedes.blogspot.de reproduction (a different host, not yet used this pass, still subject to the good-citizen one-request-at-a-time rule) to independently re-transcribe the six lines and check for the hard-to-read-letter errors the source itself flags; this is a precondition for trusting any downstream test, per rule 2. Cost $2.

3. If the abbreviation hypothesis (test 1) is rejected, run a monoalphabetic/homophonic substitution anneal against German and Latin separately (both plausible for a 16th-century Salzburg-region text), judged with matched controls at the same N and K, same solver. Cost $2-3.
matched_control: not yet run; test 3 above specifies the design if needed (synthetic German and Latin plaintext, same N/K, same solver) -- but test 1 (abbreviation hypothesis) should run first since a scribal-abbreviation reading would make a substitution-cipher control comparison the wrong test entirely (CLAUDE.md rule 3: match the design)

cheap_test_done.method: abbreviation-hypothesis pattern count (1-3 letters + period) vs synthetic control drawn i.i.d. from the target's own unigram character distribution, same length, 500 trials, seed 20260925 -- specs/cheap-tests/untersberg-code/test1_abbreviation.py
cheap_test_done.verdict: target ABOVE control range -- short-token/period clustering exceeds chance; supports the abbreviation-shaped reading over 'meaningless periods' but does not itself distinguish a real 16th-c. abbreviation convention from another structured design (no abbreviation-convention corpus on hand to test against directly). Not a reading, not closed-negative: control-backed positive signal only. See specs/cheap-tests/untersberg-code/README.md.

cheap_test_done.test: NEAR step 1 (not a spec cheap_tests_in_order test; NEAR.md's named next step after test 1 above)
cheap_test_done.method: abbreviation-expander beam search (word bigram + unigram backoff) over tools/data/de16 (Early New High German, model-written, era-plausible stand-in; no Latin corpus wired), controlled first per rule 3: 5 synthetic 71-token windows built from real de16 text abbreviated by suspension to the target's own token-length and digit-token shape (leave-window-out training). specs/cheap-tests/untersberg-code/{expand_lib.py,run_control.py,run_target.py,README.md}.
cheap_test_done.target_result: top expansion of the real 6 lines: 44/61 letter-tokens got a beam candidate (17 no vocabulary match, grade I), rest grade M (rule 4, no H/C/S possible). judge_plaintext.py specs/untersberg-code.json FAIL length (got=240, min=90, max=130) and FAIL language (score=-1.169 vs real_p05=-0.464) -- judging a self-chosen expansion with the de judge is circular and this FAIL counts for little either way (stated per brief).
cheap_test_done.verdict: Control clears its stated 0.30 gate, but the floor (shuffled word order, same expander) is only 0.032 below the control mean and the two distributions overlap heavily -- most of the control's score likely comes from prefix-matching a small repetitive vocabulary, not real bigram context; a weak pass, not strong evidence an expander would work on a harder period corpus. Target's own top expansion is not fluent and is not a reading (rule 5 near-solve amendment: partial, not closed-negative; NEAR.md is the orchestrator's file, not edited here). One-line suggestion: a real (non-model-written) Latin or German period corpus, and an abbreviation-convention word list (Cappelli/Grun) instead of generic prose vocabulary, would be the next lever if this line is pursued.

cheap_test_done.test: NEAR step 2 (not a spec cheap_tests_in_order test; source-location, not a cryptanalytic test)
cheap_test_done.method: Located Wilhelm Herzog 1929 (Die Untersbergsage nach den Handschriften, Graz-Wien-Leipzig) in full, unrestricted, via archive.org advancedsearch (identifier herzog_untersbergsage, not access-restricted); read the six-line inscription printed p.28 under 'Bild 2' (Handschrift 1, the museum's own cited pp.27-50) and confirmed it is Hs 1 = Hs 2398 via Herzog's 1928 companion article (28-leaf Salzburg Municipal Museum picture-manuscript, matching leaf count). Also confirmed the manuscript leaf: Salzburg Museum Sammlung Online opening 11 (media dc46a099-dee5-42d5-857c-bd97c80315ab), fetched at native 4884x3052 to ciphers/untersberg-code/images/hs2398_opening11_inscription_leaf.jpg -- an earlier candidate (opening 27) is ruled out.
cheap_test_done.result: Not a reading (H/C/S/M/I all 0). Herzog's own footnote states his six printed lines are a diplomatic line- and punctuation-faithful copy of Hs 1's inscription, not an emendation or decipherment. New find: Herzog's critical apparatus (p.28-29) gives the SAME inscription as it survives in 11 other manuscript witnesses, two of which (Hs 12, Hs 13) are mostly or wholly legible Latin ('Bellum. Famus. Gestas. Res. Mores. Amicus. Orpheus.' at Hs 12) and three (Hs 3, 3a, 11) give short initial-letter runs sharing letters with Hs 1's own line-2 token 'Satrnrop'. See ciphers/untersberg-code/NOTES.md 'Herzog 1929 located...' section for the full apparatus transcription and the ruled-out/confirmed leaf images.
cheap_test_done.verdict: Source-location and leaf-identification pass, not a cryptanalytic test -- status stays open/partial (rule 5). Strongest next step per this pass: a comparative philological alignment of Hs 1's inscription against Herzog's Hs 3/3a/11/12/13 variants, not a substitution anneal.

cheap_test_done.test: NEAR step (3b) (not a spec cheap_tests_in_order test; joint alignment named by NEAR.md's next-step column after bUNT5)
cheap_test_done.method: Extended bUNT5's single-witness (Hs 12) line-level alignment to a token-level, multi-witness (Hs 13, Hs 3, Hs 3a, Hs 11) joint alignment over Hs 1's flat, ordered 61-token letter sequence (line boundaries dropped, since Herzog's apparatus lineation for these four witnesses does not correspond 1:1 to Hs 1's six physical lines the way Hs 12's six words did). For each witness, a sliding best-offset search over Hs 1's sequence scored initial-letter matches (case-insensitive; the two 'eth' suspension-glyph tokens never match) and flagged any witness token that strictly extends (case-insensitive prefix of) its aligned Hs 1 token as an expansion candidate. Joint target score = sum of the four witnesses' best-offset match counts. Control (rule 3): identical procedure re-run on 500 random shuffles of Hs 1's 61-token order (seed 20260925, same seed family as this target's prior controls). specs/cheap-tests/untersberg-code/align_joint.py, align_joint_output.txt.
cheap_test_done.target: 11/52 joint initial-letter matches (Hs13 2/19 at offset 7, Hs3 3/11 at offset 5, Hs3a 3/11 at offset 5, Hs11 3/11 at offset 5) = 0.212
cheap_test_done.verdict: Joint alignment does NOT clear its own control -- 11/52 sits at the 70th percentile of 500 shuffles and 59.6% of shuffles tie or beat it, indistinguishable from chance (same conclusion as bUNT5's single-witness Hs12 test, now confirmed across all four remaining witnesses at once). Two expansion candidates were flagged at Hs13's best offset (Hs1 'P' <- Hs13 'peseit'; Hs1 'm' <- Hs13 'Moesque') but that offset itself is not control-backed (2/19 is below even the joint mean), so per rule 4 neither counts toward a C or M grade -- 0 tokens graded C or M from this test, same as bUNT5. This closes the philological-collation line for this target: neither the single strongest witness (Hs12, spelled out) nor the joint four-witness alignment beats chance. Status stays open/partial (rule 5's near-solve amendment; NEAR.md is the orchestrator's file, not edited here).
